attributes.name: [GCP GKE OTel] Deployment replica availability 99.5% rolling 30 days
attributes.description: Tracks the share of 5-minute slices in which each Kubernetes Deployment has all its desired replicas available, per Deployment (GCP project, location, cluster, namespace and Deployment name). A slice is good when the highest kube_deployment_status_replicas_available value in the slice reaches the highest kube_deployment_spec_replicas value in the slice, so a Deployment that stays short of its desired replicas for the whole slice always makes the slice bad, even while it scales up or down. Each gauge is aggregated on its own, because GKE writes them as separate documents, and maximums are not skewed by kube state metrics being sampled every 30 seconds. Crash loops, failed image pulls, Pending pods (not enough capacity, quota, unsatisfiable scheduling constraints), stuck rollouts and slow rescheduling after node loss show up as sustained shortfalls; rolling updates and scale-ups that restore full availability within the slice don't use budget. Deployments scaled to zero count as good. The objective is 99.5% of slices over a rolling 30-day window, about 3.6 hours of sustained shortfall per Deployment per month. Needs Managed Service for Prometheus kube state metrics (DEPLOYMENT component); clusters without them have no SLO instances. Excludes system namespaces, because kube state metrics are not collected for them. Limitations: available means the pod has passed its readiness probe, so a Deployment without a meaningful readiness probe can look available while the application fails. A replica that crash-loops but is ready in any sample of a slice counts as available for that slice, so intermittent crash loops are under-counted; container restart alerts cover them. Rollouts that keep replicas unavailable for more than 5 minutes (large Deployments, slow-starting pods) use budget; setting maxUnavailable to 0 avoids this. A scale-up that is still in progress when a slice ends makes that slice bad, so Deployments that autoscale often and start slowly use some budget. Slices without data, for example while kube state metrics collection is interrupted, count as good, so a broken collection pipeline looks healthy. Every Deployment outside system namespaces becomes an SLO instance; add a namespace filter to limit the SLO to production workloads. Data delay: the receiver polls Cloud Monitoring on an interval, so the latest minutes can be incomplete and burn rates lag real time by a few minutes. Set the SLO sync delay to at least 5 minutes so late documents are not skipped.
